stories.title: Wire the F-092/097/111 card emitters to EXECUTE + write state (carousel data-starvation root fix)
acceptance: PRE-FLIGHT: on the Pi, confirm the starting state -- /run/eclipse-obd/states/ contains only boot-state; no emitter service units installed (baseline the bug before fixing)

wire each of system_status_emitter / battery_health_emitter / dtc_emitter to EXECUTE on the Pi (systemd unit(s) mirroring eclipse-boot-state.service, and/or orchestrator invocation, per Atlas's run-model ruling); each writes its state file to the states dir the eclipse-states-http server reads
on the Pi, the states dir contains system-status + battery-health + dtc files, freshly written + refreshing on cadence; eclipse-states-http serves them (HTTP 200 + non-empty JSON)
the dtc emitter writes an honest empty/absent state when no code + no key-on read (so takeoverView() correctly renders nothing -- the phantom Check Engine disappears)
Typecheck + pi tests green for this slice

validationCriteria.action: load the carousel on the Pi parked (no OBD)
validationCriteria.outcome: cards render honest state; NO phantom Check Engine takeover

conditionalOutcomes: RUN-MODEL is an Atlas call (Iris Q-1): standalone systemd units (like boot-state) vs orchestrator-invoked vs a single emitter supervisor. Route to Atlas for the ruling BEFORE building if it's not an obvious mirror of eclipse-boot-state.service. Iris's coupled Q-1 (idle as an emitter-written boolean vs display-derived) rides this ruling.
if an emitter needs live OBD to write meaningful data (dtc KOEO read), it must still write an HONEST absent/asleep state when parked -- never nothing, never fabricated
stories.goal: As the deployed carousel, I want the system-status / battery-health / dtc emitters to actually RUN and write their state files on the Pi, so the cards render live data instead of starving (which leaves the static DTC takeover visible = phantom 'Check Engine'). ROOT CAUSE (PM-verified on the live Pi @ V0.29.14): /run/eclipse-obd/states/ holds ONLY boot-state; only eclipse-boot-state.service + eclipse-states-http.service run -- there is NO service unit for system_status_emitter/battery_health_emitter/dtc_emitter and the orchestrator does not invoke them. The emitter CODE shipped (F-092/097/111) but was never wired to execute. (Split from US-480; this is the RUNTIME half -- deploy-install is US-480-b.)

stories.title: Idle-state home card -- calm honest parked view (pairs with US-480)
acceptance: idle card renders per Iris spec §1.2: header (wordmark+clock+date), STANDBY hero (neutral grey) + 'engine off / OBD asleep' substate, 3-fact summary strip (last-drive / battery-with-age / honest-faults), footer

idle detection derived from existing SSOT (spec §1.4): idle == system-status.source.obd.available==false AND drive.state==idle -- pure consumer, no new data acquisition (UNLESS Atlas rules the emitter should write an explicit idle flag per US-480 conditionalOutcome / Iris Q-1)
carousel makes idle the HOME card while idle holds, and AUTO-ADVANCES off idle to System-Status/live the moment OBD wakes or a drive records (Iris AC-4)

honest-instrument rules (spec §1.3): never green 'OK' at idle (STANDBY grey; green only on the battery line with its age); never amber/red at idle unless a REAL stored STOP/WATCH code exists (then the existing ribbon/takeover still wins -- idle never suppresses a real fault, Iris AC-5); absence != clean and != fault
uses specs/UI/tokens.css SSOT values (not the drifted dashboard.css literals -- see US-484)
Argus-style AC 1/2/3/4/5 from Iris spec §4 pass; pi/UI tests green

validationCriteria.outcome: idle card is the home card; STANDBY grey; faults line 'DTC not read since key-off'; no false green

validationCriteria.outcome: ribbon/takeover surfaces the real fault (idle does not suppress it)

stories.goal: As the CIO parked with the engine off, I want a calm, honest home card instead of a wall of NA/unavailable tiles (which reads as broken and is the backdrop the phantom alarm appears against). Per Iris's CIO-locked spec (§1): STANDBY (neutral grey, never green) + clock/date + last-drive + battery (stale-green 'checked Nd ago' guard) + honest faults line ('DTC not read since key-off' -- NOT 'No codes', NOT 'Check Engine'). The parked twin of the EDR-gated live home card (same home slot).

stories.title: Light-feed brightness consumer -- auto-dim from a `light` lux state file + honest fixed fallback + alarm floor
acceptance: display reads light.lux (+ freshness) from the `light` state file; brightness = clamp(MIN, curve(lux), 1.0) -- curve is Iris's (UI), lux value is the reader's (owner = the single dedicated EDR reader, per Atlas DELTA-2 pure-consumer ruling)

ALARM FLOOR (load-bearing): MIN never dims the screen below a legible threshold while a REAL active alarm (STOP ribbon/takeover) is present -- dim a calm idle screen, never a damage-in-progress warning; the floor is a UI guard independent of lux

HONEST FALLBACK: until the `light` state file exists / is fresh, hold a fixed default brightness + show NO fabricated 'auto' behavior (honest instrument) -- do not pretend to react to light it can't read
Iris AC-7: brightness tracks a fresh light.lux; absent/stale -> fixed default (no fake auto); dimming never takes a STOP alarm below its legible floor
consumes the state file only -- no hardware polling in the display; pi/UI tests green

validationCriteria.outcome: fixed default brightness, no fake 'auto' indicator

validationCriteria.action: inject a fresh light.lux state file
STOP alarm present + lux says dark
validationCriteria.outcome: brightness held at/above the legible alarm floor

conditionalOutcomes: GATED on Atlas Q-4: the `light` lux state-file contract (state-file seam + fallback-when-absent). Do NOT finalize the contract shape before Atlas blesses it. The near-term fixed-fallback slice is buildable now; the live-lux consumption lands with the EDR reader (W-9).
stories.goal: As the display, I want brightness driven by a live lux reading (pure consumer of a `light` state file the EDR light reader owns), not a clock schedule -- CIO-confirmed 2026-07-21 the light sensor is a real data feed. The display never reads the sensor itself. Live lux is EDR-gated (TSL2591, W-9); near-term ships an HONEST fixed-default fallback (no fake 'auto' when the state file is absent/stale).
